title: Launch Orpheus (probe console), then watch its feed (starboard screen)

text: Orpheus is loaded at the probe console. Its feed will show on the starboard screen.

title: Launch Orpheus (probe console), then watch its feed (starboard screen)

text: There it goes. The shadow's bigger every frame.
When it passes 1.33 rₛ, where we hovered, will its picture go all black like our window did?

No. Hovering there, the shadow covered 207 degrees of our sky. Orpheus will pass that spot at 85% of light speed, and its motion swings the sky ahead of it. It will see the shadow only 79 degrees across.
Same place, different motion, different sky.
Frames are arriving further apart. The signal is being stretched as it climbs out.
(That view. That's what I dreamt.)
No more frames are coming. The next one was due from inside the horizon, and nothing sent from there gets out. Its marker in the window is fading: its last light is still climbing, slower and redder.
So that last frame is all we get. Did it fall in, or is it stuck there?
And the rest of the trip, the part inside... nobody out here will ever see it.
No one outside ever will. Only Orpheus saw it.
(Only Orpheus. And me, in a dream.)

title: Frozen Star
subtitle: Thanks for playing. The Tern is yours to explore.

text: Doctor, one item is left on the survey plan, if you want it. It is optional. A ranging-laser test at the photon sphere.

title: Optional: take the Tern down to the photon sphere, 1.5 rₛ (helm)

text: The what sphere?
One and a half horizon radii. At that height light can orbit Erebus. A beam fired sideways goes all the way round.
Light going in a circle. Okay, doc, I have to see that.

title: Optional: take the Tern down to the photon sphere, 1.5 rₛ (helm)
Photon sphere reached. Listen to WREN's briefing

text: Photon sphere. I have locked the field to it, to within a centimetre. You will see why that matters.
Look forward: the shadow now covers exactly half the sky, 180 degrees. Its edge is a circle at right angles to our nose: straight up, straight down, and straight out on either side of the hull.

title: Photon sphere reached. Listen to WREN's briefing
Fire the ranging laser along the hull (helm)

text: Pulse away. Watch the plot on the helm panel.

title: Watch the pulse go round Erebus (helm panel)
Fire the ranging laser along the hull (helm)

text: Caught at the stern, 11.1 seconds after it left, 2.7 metres from where it set out. It went all the way round Erebus: 3.34 million km.

title: Watch the pulse go round Erebus (helm panel)

text: As you predicted. That is just the circumference divided by the speed of light.
Wait. So any light that leaves the ship sideways comes back round to us?
